title: The Most Employable Technical People Aren't the Best Builders
author: Mike Watson
summary: Mike Watson, a veteran fintech product manager, argues that the technical professionals who survive repeated rounds of layoffs and stay visible to leadership are not necessarily the best builders — they are the best translators across organizational languages. Through a personal story of running an affiliate-marketing implementation at an auto-refi startup, where he had to learn the domain himself and stand between a VP and engineers who could not talk to each other, he shows that translation — restating a business need in engineering terms and vice versa — is what makes a person's contribution legible in the rooms where staffing decisions get made. His central formulation is that when two different leaders can describe your contribution in their own terms you exist in two rooms; when only one can, you exist in one; when neither can, you are a line item — 'the math layoffs run on.' Crucially, he insists translation is not a personality trait but a set of small, learnable habits — translating up, down, and sideways — that build legibility over time.
points: The technical people who stay employable through layoff cycles are the best translators, not the best builders — up to leadership, down to engineers, sideways across teams.
Translation makes a contribution legible: 'When two different leaders can describe what you contributed in their own terms, you exist in two different rooms.'
Invisibility to decision-makers, not poor work, is what quietly sinks capable people: 'That’s the math layoffs run on, whether anyone says it out loud or not.'
Translation is not a personality trait but a set of small, learnable habits — translate up (lead with what's possible), down (reshape vague asks), and sideways (name mismatched vocabulary).

Done consistently, translation changes how leaders describe you — from 'does data infrastructure' to 'keeps marketing and engineering pointed at the same problem' — the description that survives a spreadsheet.
quotes: The technical people I’ve watched stay employable through every cycle aren’t the best builders. They’re the best translators.
When two different leaders can describe what you contributed in their own terms, you exist in two different rooms. When only one can, you exist in one. When neither can, you’re a line item.
Doing the work is necessary and not sufficient. The people who decide your fate often don’t speak your language.
The good news about translation is that it isn’t a personality trait. It’s a set of habits, and most of them are small enough to start practicing this week.
When leadership asks for something hard, lead with what’s possible inside the constraint, not the constraint itself.
